notes: §1985:X.5.3.4 GR1 requires that 'Literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 identifies the program to be cancelled.' CallBinder#BindCancel binds each operand (refusing a numeric or edited identifier, COBOL1696, and a numeric literal or figurative, COBOL1627), CallEmitter#EmitCancel renders the literal or the identifier's value at execution in the edition's spelling, and ProgramTable#Cancel forms the externalized name and locates the program through ResolveVisible, the same scope CALL uses. Probes at --std 85: an X(8) identifier holding 'SUBP' with trailing spaces, a ref-modified identifier at (1:4), a group identifier and a two-literal CANCEL each reset the named program (counts 2 to 1 on the next CALL); a never-called and a nonexistent name took no action; a lowercase literal cancelled SUBP; national and PROGRAM-POINTER operands were refused (COBOL0900, 2002+). The witness cancels through an identifier and re-calls the program in its initial state.

next.reason: 1985: 'Literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 identifies the program to be cancelled.' §2023:14.9.5.4 GR1 keeps both and adds 'c) program-prototype-name-1', and sends the literal/identifier value through 8.3.2.2, where under the COBOL call convention 'the program-name is treated as a COBOL word that maps to the externalized name of the program' (§2023:8.3.2.2). A 1985 CANCEL means the same; the rule is looser (a third operand kind, national identifiers).
